chart.title: International Phonetic Alphabet in IPA Kiel (IPA Chart), sub-chart 'VOWELS'
chart.revision: IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005; current annual re-issue printed '© 2026 IPA' (vowel sub-chart footer: 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'). Per the IPA page, 2018 and 2020 issues were identical to the 2015/2005 revision apart from years and copyright symbols, and since 2025 the chart is re-issued annually.
chart.licence: Copyright International Phonetic Association; available under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-SA 4.0).
chart.how_read: Opened the IPA chart page (revision history and licence text). The full-chart PDF (IPA_Kiel.pdf) could not be read as text, so I viewed the official vowel sub-chart image IPA_Kiel_V_0600.png from the IPA site and read the 28 symbols, row labels, the pairing note and the footer from it. Cross-checked symbols, descriptions, IPA names, IPA numbers and Unicode values against the IPA's own tooltip-chart data file (IPAcharts/IPA_charts_TI/dbs/arrays.js, entries with Tbl:5, SID 501-528, exactly 28). Unicode names checked against unicode.org UnicodeData.txt (latest) and Python unicodedata.

count_explanation: The vowel trapezium prints 28 symbols: close row 6 (i y ɨ ʉ ɯ u), near-close 3 (ɪ ʏ ʊ), close-mid 6 (e ø ɘ ɵ ɤ o), mid 1 (ə), open-mid 6 (ɛ œ ɜ ɞ ʌ ɔ), near-open 2 (æ ɐ), open 4 (a ɶ ɑ ɒ). The IPA's tooltip-chart database lists exactly 28 entries for the vowel table (SID 501-528), matching the image. No vowel symbol on the chart is a diacritic or a two-representation case, so no equivalent_to links. Not counted: rhotacized ɚ/ɝ (not printed in the trapezium; ˞ belongs to diacritics), retired symbols (ı ɩ ɷ ʚ etc.), and the near-front/near-back labels (positions, not symbols).

acoustic_correlates.text: Lowest F1 class on the chart (close). Highest F2 of all vowels (front, unrounded), with F3 also high and close to F2. Reference point for the top-left corner of the F1/F2 plane.
Catford's average values for a male voice: F1 240 Hz, F2 2400 Hz (F2-F1 = 2160 Hz). Phonetician's cardinal-style reference values, single adult male voice type; no F3 given in this table.

American English men's average for the vowel listed as /i/ 'beet': F1 270 Hz, F2 2290 Hz, F3 3010 Hz. This is a language-specific vowel near [i], not a cardinal [i]; use as an order-of-magnitude check, not a target.

symbols.notes: Primary cardinal vowel 1. Not to be confused with U+0131 LATIN SMALL LETTER DOTLESS I (IPA 394, retired).

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 about as low as [i] (close). F2 and F3 both lower than for [i]: front rounding lowers F2 and F3, which is the main acoustic cue separating [y] from [i]; F2 still well above any central or back vowel.
Catford's average values for a male voice: F1 235 Hz, F2 2100 Hz (F2-F1 = 1865 Hz). Phonetician's cardinal-style reference values, single adult male voice type; no F3 given in this table.

symbols.notes: Secondary cardinal vowel 9.

symbols.unicode_name: LATIN SMALL LETTER I WITH STROKE

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 low, like [i] and [u] (close). F2 intermediate: below [i]/[y] and above [ɯ]/[u] (central). Unrounded, so F2 should sit above that of its rounded partner [ʉ].
No fetched source gave hertz values for this vowel; only the relative expectations above are supported.

symbols.notes: Not to be confused with U+0197 (capital I with stroke) or with i + combining stroke.

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 low (close). F2 central, lower than [ɨ] because of rounding but higher than [u]; F3 also lowered relative to [ɨ].
No fetched source gave hertz values for this vowel; only the relative expectations above are supported.

symbols.notes: Single precomposed character; do not compose u + U+0336.

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 low (close). F2 low (back) but clearly higher than [u], because without lip rounding the back cavity is not lengthened; F2 tends toward the central region.
Catford's average values for a male voice: F1 300 Hz, F2 1390 Hz (F2-F1 = 1090 Hz). Phonetician's cardinal-style reference values, single adult male voice type; no F3 given in this table.

symbols.notes: Secondary cardinal vowel 16.

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 low (close; rounding in back vowels lowers F1 further). F2 among the lowest on the chart (back + rounded), so F1 and F2 are close together; F3 relatively low.
Catford's average values for a male voice: F1 250 Hz, F2 595 Hz (F2-F1 = 345 Hz). Phonetician's cardinal-style reference values, single adult male voice type; no F3 given in this table.

American English men's average for the vowel listed as /u/ 'boot': F1 300 Hz, F2 870 Hz, F3 2240 Hz. This is a language-specific vowel near [u], not a cardinal [u]; use as an order-of-magnitude check, not a target.

symbols.notes: Primary cardinal vowel 8.

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 somewhat higher than [i] (slightly lower tongue). F2 somewhat lower than [i] (slightly retracted from front). Lies between [i] and [e] on the F1 axis.

American English men's average for the vowel listed as /I/ 'bit': F1 390 Hz, F2 1990 Hz, F3 2550 Hz. This is a language-specific vowel near [ɪ], not a cardinal [ɪ]; use as an order-of-magnitude check, not a target.

symbols.notes: Small capital I. Not U+0049 'I' and not U+0269 LATIN SMALL LETTER IOTA (IPA 399, retired).

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 somewhat higher than [y]; F2 somewhat lower than [y]. Compared with [ɪ], F2 and F3 are lower because of rounding.
No fetched source gave hertz values for this vowel; only the relative expectations above are supported.

symbols.notes: Small capital Y; not U+0059.

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 somewhat higher than [u]; F2 somewhat higher than [u] (less back). Rounded, so F2 below that of an unrounded vowel at the same position.

American English men's average for the vowel listed as /U/ 'book': F1 440 Hz, F2 1020 Hz, F3 2240 Hz. This is a language-specific vowel near [ʊ], not a cardinal [ʊ]; use as an order-of-magnitude check, not a target.

symbols.notes: Upsilon; not Greek U+03C5 υ and not U+0277 LATIN SMALL LETTER CLOSED OMEGA (IPA 398, retired).

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 higher than [i]/[ɪ], lower than [ɛ] (close-mid). F2 high, a little below [i] (front, unrounded).
Catford's average values for a male voice: F1 390 Hz, F2 2300 Hz (F2-F1 = 1910 Hz). Phonetician's cardinal-style reference values, single adult male voice type; no F3 given in this table.

symbols.notes: Primary cardinal vowel 2.

symbols.unicode_name: LATIN SMALL LETTER O WITH STROKE

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 like [e] (close-mid). F2 and F3 lower than for [e] (front rounding), F2 still above central vowels.
Catford's average values for a male voice: F1 370 Hz, F2 1900 Hz (F2-F1 = 1530 Hz). Phonetician's cardinal-style reference values, single adult male voice type; no F3 given in this table.

symbols.notes: Secondary cardinal vowel 10. Not U+2205 EMPTY SET.

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 close-mid, between [ɨ] and [ə]. F2 central: below [e]/[ø], above [ɤ]/[o]; above its rounded partner [ɵ].
No fetched source gave hertz values for this vowel; only the relative expectations above are supported.

symbols.notes: One of the 1990s additions numbered downward from 399 (IPA 397, per the 'IPA number' page). Not U+01DD (turned e) and not schwa U+0259.

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 close-mid. F2 central and lower than [ɘ] (rounding); F3 lowered relative to [ɘ].
No fetched source gave hertz values for this vowel; only the relative expectations above are supported.

symbols.notes: Not U+03B8 Greek theta (consonant symbol θ) nor U+0473/U+04E9 Cyrillic barred o.

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 close-mid, like [o]. F2 low-ish (back) but clearly higher than [o] because unrounded; F2 drifts toward the central region.
Catford's average values for a male voice: F1 460 Hz, F2 1310 Hz (F2-F1 = 850 Hz). Phonetician's cardinal-style reference values, single adult male voice type; no F3 given in this table.

symbols.notes: Ram's horns. Classic trap: not U+0263 LATIN SMALL LETTER GAMMA (ɣ, voiced velar fricative). The IPA's glyph notes ask for 'more distinct ram's horns' in this glyph. Secondary cardinal vowel 15.

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 close-mid, higher than [u], lower than [ɔ]. F2 low (back + rounded), close to F1.
Catford's average values for a male voice: F1 360 Hz, F2 640 Hz (F2-F1 = 280 Hz). Phonetician's cardinal-style reference values, single adult male voice type; no F3 given in this table.

symbols.notes: Primary cardinal vowel 7.

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 and F2 both mid-range: F1 between close-mid and open-mid vowels, F2 between front and back vowels. Commonly treated as the vowel of the neutral (approximately uniform) vocal tract, whose formants are roughly evenly spaced.
A uniform tube of adult male vocal-tract length (17 cm) has formants near F1 500 Hz, F2 1500 Hz, F3 2500 Hz; these are the textbook neutral-tract values.
Identifying [ə] with that neutral tube is the usual textbook simplification; the page read does not itself make that link.

symbols.notes: Height/backness 'mid central'; the IPA description gives no rounding value. Not U+01DD LATIN SMALL LETTER TURNED E and not U+04D9 Cyrillic schwa. Rhotacized ɚ (U+025A, IPA 327) is not printed in the vowel trapezium.

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 higher than [e], lower than [æ]/[a] (open-mid). F2 high, below [e] (front unrounded; F2 of front vowels falls as they open).
Catford's average values for a male voice: F1 610 Hz, F2 1900 Hz (F2-F1 = 1290 Hz). Phonetician's cardinal-style reference values, single adult male voice type; no F3 given in this table.

American English men's average for the vowel listed as /e/ 'bet': F1 530 Hz, F2 1840 Hz, F3 2480 Hz. This is a language-specific vowel near [ɛ], not a cardinal [ɛ]; use as an order-of-magnitude check, not a target.

symbols.notes: Primary cardinal vowel 3. Not Greek U+03B5 ε.

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 like [ɛ] (open-mid). F2 and F3 lower than for [ɛ] (front rounding).
Catford's average values for a male voice: F1 585 Hz, F2 1710 Hz (F2-F1 = 1125 Hz). Phonetician's cardinal-style reference values, single adult male voice type; no F3 given in this table.

symbols.notes: Secondary cardinal vowel 11.

symbols.unicode_name: LATIN SMALL LETTER REVERSED OPEN E

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 open-mid, like [ɛ] and [ʌ]. F2 central: between [ɛ] and [ʌ]; above its rounded partner [ɞ].
No fetched source gave hertz values for this vowel; only the relative expectations above are supported.

symbols.notes: Not U+0437 Cyrillic ze or digit 3. Rhotacized ɝ (U+025D) is not printed in the trapezium.

symbols.unicode_name: LATIN SMALL LETTER CLOSED REVERSED OPEN E

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 open-mid. F2 central and lower than [ɜ]; F3 lowered relative to [ɜ] (rounding).
No fetched source gave hertz values for this vowel; only the relative expectations above are supported.

symbols.notes: One of the 1990s additions numbered downward from 399 (IPA 395, per the 'IPA number' page). Not U+029A LATIN SMALL LETTER CLOSED OPEN E (ʚ, IPA 396), which is not on the current chart.

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 open-mid, like [ɔ]. F2 low (back) but well above [ɔ] because unrounded.
Catford's average values for a male voice: F1 600 Hz, F2 1170 Hz (F2-F1 = 570 Hz). Phonetician's cardinal-style reference values, single adult male voice type; no F3 given in this table.

American English men's average for the vowel listed as /L/ 'but': F1 640 Hz, F2 1190 Hz, F3 2390 Hz. This is a language-specific vowel near [ʌ], not a cardinal [ʌ]; use as an order-of-magnitude check, not a target.

symbols.notes: Secondary cardinal vowel 14. Not Greek U+039B Λ.

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 open-mid, higher than [o], lower than [ɒ]/[ɑ]. F2 low (back + rounded), close to F1.
Catford's average values for a male voice: F1 500 Hz, F2 700 Hz (F2-F1 = 200 Hz). Phonetician's cardinal-style reference values, single adult male voice type; no F3 given in this table.

American English men's average for the vowel listed as /aw/ 'bought': F1 570 Hz, F2 840 Hz, F3 2410 Hz. This is a language-specific vowel near [ɔ], not a cardinal [ɔ]; use as an order-of-magnitude check, not a target.

symbols.notes: Primary cardinal vowel 6.

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 higher than [ɛ], a little lower than [a] (near-open). F2 front: below [ɛ] and above central vowels.

American English men's average for the vowel listed as /ae/ 'bat': F1 660 Hz, F2 1720 Hz, F3 2410 Hz. This is a language-specific vowel near [æ], not a cardinal [æ]; use as an order-of-magnitude check, not a target.

symbols.notes: Not a cardinal vowel; printed between open-mid and open on the front edge.

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 high, between [ɜ]/[ə] and [a] (near-open). F2 central, between [æ] and [ɑ].
No fetched source gave hertz values for this vowel; only the relative expectations above are supported.

symbols.notes: IPA description 'near-open central vowel' gives no rounding value. Printed on the central line between open-mid and open.

acoustic_correlates.text: Highest F1 class on the chart (open front). F2 lower than the other front vowels (F2 of front vowels falls as they open) but above back [ɑ]/[ɒ].
Catford's average values for a male voice: F1 850 Hz, F2 1610 Hz (F2-F1 = 760 Hz). Phonetician's cardinal-style reference values, single adult male voice type; no F3 given in this table.

symbols.notes: Primary cardinal vowel 4. Must be the two-storey 'a' U+0061 as distinct from script ɑ U+0251; fonts that draw U+0061 single-storey hide the contrast.

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 high, like [a] (open). F2 a little lower than [a] (rounding), the smallest front-rounding effect on the chart because the open jaw limits lip rounding.
Catford's average values for a male voice: F1 820 Hz, F2 1530 Hz (F2-F1 = 710 Hz). Phonetician's cardinal-style reference values, single adult male voice type; no F3 given in this table.

symbols.notes: Secondary cardinal vowel 12. Small capital OE ligature, not U+0152 Œ.

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 high (open). F2 low (back), so F1 and F2 lie close together; above its rounded partner [ɒ].
Catford's average values for a male voice: F1 750 Hz, F2 940 Hz (F2-F1 = 190 Hz). Phonetician's cardinal-style reference values, single adult male voice type; no F3 given in this table.

American English men's average for the vowel listed as /a/ 'father': F1 730 Hz, F2 1090 Hz, F3 2440 Hz. This is a language-specific vowel near [ɑ], not a cardinal [ɑ]; use as an order-of-magnitude check, not a target.

symbols.notes: Primary cardinal vowel 5. Not Greek U+03B1 α, and distinct from 'a' U+0061.

acoustic_correlates.text: F1 high (open), slightly below [ɑ] (rounding lowers F1 in back vowels). F2 lower than [ɑ]; F1 and F2 almost merge.
Catford's average values for a male voice: F1 700 Hz, F2 760 Hz (F2-F1 = 60 Hz). Phonetician's cardinal-style reference values, single adult male voice type; no F3 given in this table.

symbols.notes: Secondary cardinal vowel 13.

problems: The full official chart PDF (IPA_Kiel.pdf) could not be read as text here (no PDF renderer); the vowel section was read from the official sub-chart PNG plus the IPA's own tooltip-chart data file, which agree.

Revision naming: the printed chart says 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005' with copyright year 2026; earlier issues were labelled 2018 and 2020 but are the same revision. The brief's '2015 chart as revised' is that revision.

Formant numbers are secondary: Catford (2001) values were read only as quoted on Wikipedia 'Formant' (male voice, 16 of 28 vowels, F1/F2 only), and Peterson & Barney (1952) values only as quoted on a Princeton course page (American English men, 9 vowels mapped by me from ASCII labels: /e/ 'bet' -> ɛ, /a/ 'father' -> ɑ, /aw/ 'bought' -> ɔ, /L/ 'but' -> ʌ, /U/ 'book' -> ʊ, /ae/ 'bat' -> æ, /I/ 'bit' -> ɪ). The P&B vowels are English phonemes, not cardinal qualities (e.g. American 'but' is more central than cardinal ʌ).

No fetched source gave hertz values for ɨ ʉ ʏ ɘ ɵ ɜ ɞ ɐ (or F3 for most vowels); those carry relational correlates only. Attempts to open sources with cardinal-vowel formants of Daniel Jones (Vaissière 2011, HAL) were blocked by an access-denied page, and Jassem & Krzyśko 1992 'In quest for Cardinal Vowels' (Archives of Acoustics) full text could not be read.

Wikipedia 'Phonetic symbols in Unicode' was fetched but the tool's summary returned wrong character names (e.g. 'LATIN LETTER REVERSED I' for U+0268); it was discarded and names were taken from unicode.org UnicodeData.txt and the IPA's own data instead.
ə and ɐ: the IPA descriptions ('mid central vowel', 'near-open central vowel') give no rounding value; features.rounding is 'unspecified'.

The relational F1/F2/F3 statements per vowel are my own application of the general rules in wiki_formant, wiki_vowel and umanitoba_formants (height ~ inverse F1, backness ~ F2, rounding lowers F2/F3 in front vowels and F1/F2 in back vowels); the specific neighbour-by-neighbour orderings (e.g. ɶ having a small rounding effect, ɯ F2 drifting toward central) are inferences, not quoted findings.

Confusable code points named in notes (U+0131, U+0263, U+0269, U+0277, U+029A, U+01DD, U+03B1, U+03B5, U+03C5, U+2205 etc.) were checked against Python's local unicodedata (Unicode 13.0) only, not a fetched page; U+0131/U+0269/U+0277/U+029A as retired IPA letters come from wiki_ipa_number.
Cardinal-vowel numbers in notes (CV1-16) are recalled-unverified; no fetched source in this session lists them.
